newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Anhui Expressway seeking H-shares listing - paper.
newsitem.headline: Anhui Expressway seeking H-shares listing - paper.

text.p: China's Anhui Expressway Co is seeking to raise HK$400 million through an H-share listing in Hong Kong, the South China Morning Post reported on Monday.

The English-language paper gave no further details but said the Anhui provincial government had guaranteed the company a "stable" income by permitting it to increase the toll on its Hening Expressway to cover inflation.

The daily quoted Anhui Expressway chairman Wang Shui as saying the toll has been doubled since the highway opened in 1991, and now stands a 0.03 yuan per tonne km for small vehicles, 0.06 for medium vehicles and 0.08 for large road users.
The 134-km Hening Expressway runs from Dashushan to Zhouzhuang and is part of the Hefei-Nanjing Expressway in eastern China.
The expressway, the company's sole asset, was developed in three phases with investment totalling 1.2 billion yuan and the last phase was completed last year, the newspaper said.

Traffic volume had risen 30 percent in the past five years to about 10,000 vehicles a day and the company expects the volume to increase 20 percent annually over the next five years to 56,000 a day at its full capacity, the daily said.
